entries.name: CLARANS clustering
entries.definition: A randomized medoid-clustering algorithm that searches fixed-size sets of representative observations by accepting improving single swaps and restarting after a budget of unsuccessful neighbor trials.
entries.identity_notes: CLARANS searches the graph of all k-object medoid sets. It samples possible swaps at each state rather than confining all medoids to a fixed subsample as CLARA does, and differs from PAM’s exhaustive best-swap search. Medoids are actual observations, unlike k-means centroids. The record covers the original 1994 clustering method, not its SD/NSD spatial data-mining wrappers or the expanded 2002 polygon-handling methods. No normalized identity match for this candidate was found across all 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 227 preceding native IDs/names/aliases. The same search identified BIRCH as an existing native record and excluded it from additions. Full-checkout word-delimited fixed-string searches included ignored and hidden files, with 79 worktree and 79 main-checkout matching lines; these concern BIRCH identity/proposal/review context and discovery leads. Ten exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms and outgoing edges, and nine neighboring native records, were inspected.
limitations: A sampled unsuccessful-trial budget does not certify a local minimum over all possible swaps or a global optimum. The paper’s quoted local-minimum terminology is a stopping heuristic.

The original pseudocode specifies a random neighbor but does not state a sampling-without-replacement rule or a particular probability law. This record does not add one, and it does not treat the trial counter as a count of distinct neighbors.

Section 2.1 describes cost contributions for currently nonselected objects before Equation (5). Interpreting that literally as excluding every current medoid can omit the removed medoid’s new assignment cost. The full-objective definition in Section 3.1 is retained; an original finite calculation demonstrates the omission, not an author-issued erratum or executed implementation.

The requested k, dissimilarity, initialization, trial budget and restart count affect the result. The paper’s experimental numlocal=2 and maxneighbor=max(250, 1.25% of k(n-k)) are experimental choices, not guarantees or identity requirements. No runtime or quality advantage is asserted.

claims.statement: For n observations, supplied dissimilarities and 1<=k<n, represent a search state by k selected observations M. Assign each observation to a nearest medoid and define F(M)=sum_(x in X)min_(m in M)d(x,m), over all n observations. A neighboring state replaces one selected medoid with one unselected observation, giving k(n-k) possible neighbors. Begin a run at an arbitrary state. Sample a random neighbor; if its total cost is strictly lower, accept it and reset the unsuccessful-trial counter. Otherwise increment that counter. After maxneighbor unsuccessful trials at the current state, compare its cost with the best completed run and restart until numlocal runs have finished. Return the lowest-cost retained state. Swaps are judged by the full objective difference, including the observation whose medoid role is removed.

entries.name: Relevant component analysis
entries.definition: A partially supervised linear metric-learning procedure that estimates within-group covariance from positive equivalence constraints and whitens the representation using that covariance.
entries.identity_notes: RCA forms chunklets from observations known to share a class without requiring their class names. Different chunklets need not represent different classes. It estimates variation within chunklets, unlike whitening by total covariance, and it does not optimize NCA’s stochastic neighbor reward. The maintained LDA record is a Gaussian classifier, not RCA or the optional constraints-based Fisher projection. This record describes batch RCA; online adaptation and optional dimensionality-reduction procedures are qualified extensions. limitations: The inverse and inverse square root require a nonsingular covariance on the represented space. Few, singleton or geometrically redundant chunklets may give a singular estimate. This record does not invent a universal pseudoinverse or regularization fallback.

Algorithm 2 calls sum_j(|C_j|-1) the covariance rank. In general it is a sample-size upper bound, not the actual rank; collinearity can leave the covariance singular even when that count exceeds the feature dimension. The preceding prose’s rank-greater-than-dimension condition is not a feasible matrix-rank requirement. The source heuristic is not copied as an invertibility guarantee.

Whitening can amplify low-variance noise, and erroneous equivalence constraints can contaminate entire chunklets through transitive closure. Small within-group variance is not itself evidence of relevance to a downstream task.

The paper’s likelihood and information-optimality results have stated modeling assumptions; this record claims neither universal classification improvement nor unconditional statistical optimality. Optional cFLD, online RCA and their implementation details require separate scope assessments. No model was trained.

claims.statement: Take the transitive closure of positive same-class constraints to obtain chunklets C_j with means m_j. Let N be the total number of observations in the chunklets, as clarified in Section 5, and compute Chat=(1/N)sum_j sum_(x in C_j)(x-m_j)(x-m_j)^T. When Chat is positive definite on the represented space, use the symmetric whitening transform W=Chat^(-1/2) on the original feature vectors. Equivalently, compare vectors with squared distance (x-y)^T Chat^(-1)(x-y). Large within-chunklet variance directions receive less weight. The method uses positive constraints without requiring explicit class labels or negative constraints. The paper permits an optional reduction before whitening and describes a constraints-based Fisher discriminant projection; nonsingularity must hold in the retained space.

entries.name: Large margin nearest neighbor
entries.definition: A supervised metric-learning method that fits a positive-semidefinite distance matrix by pulling fixed same-class target neighbors together while penalizing margin violations by differently labeled observations.
entries.identity_notes: The core single-metric LMNN formulation fixes directed target-neighbor assignments before fitting and uses a convex objective in a positive-semidefinite matrix. It is not NCA’s stochastic classification objective, a generic triplet loss, or a deep embedding network. Iteratively reassigning targets, learning local metrics, kernelization and rank constraints are distinct extensions; their behavior is not inferred from the core convex program. The energy-based prediction rule in Section 3.5 is separate from ordinary k-nearest-neighbor voting. The same search identified BIRCH as an existing native record and excluded it from additions. Ten exact AIO CLASS nodes with scoped synonyms and outgoing edges, and nine neighboring native records, were inspected.
limitations: Each point needs enough other same-class observations for its chosen target count. Target selection, labels, weighting, feature scale and the solver affect the learned representation; training margins do not certify held-out accuracy.

The source uses metric terminology for quadratic distances. The displayed d_M is a squared distance and does not itself generally satisfy the triangle inequality; its square root is a pseudometric when M is positive semidefinite and may collapse distinct points if M is rank deficient.

Convexity applies to the fixed-target optimization over M, not to arbitrary factorized, rank-constrained or target-reassignment extensions. Convexity also does not imply a unique optimum, perfect training separation or a certified result from every numerical solver.

The endpoints of the stated weight interval can remove one training term; mu=0 permits the collapsed M=0 solution. The paper’s unit margin is a scale convention. No benchmark, special-purpose solver implementation or extension was reproduced.

claims.statement: For labeled vectors choose k other same-class target neighbors T_i for each training point, usually using Euclidean distance before fitting; these directed sets remain fixed in the core method. Let d_M(i,j)=(x_i-x_j)^T M(x_i-x_j), with M positive semidefinite. Minimize (1-mu)sum_i sum_(j in T_i)d_M(i,j)+mu sum_i sum_(j in T_i)sum_(l:y_l!=y_i)max(0,1+d_M(i,j)-d_M(i,l)), with mu in [0,1]. The pull term concerns target neighbors, not all same-class pairs, and the hinge is not squared. Introducing nonnegative slack variables for the margin violations yields a semidefinite program. After learning, factor M=L^T L and use the learned distances for k-nearest-neighbor classification. The matrix-variable objective is convex for fixed target sets; optimizing directly in L is not generally convex.

native_neighbors.name: CURE clustering
native_neighbors.definition: An agglomerative clustering procedure that represents each cluster by several scattered points shrunk toward its mean and merges the pair with the smallest distance between their representative points.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: CURE uses a set of representative locations, unlike centroid-only k-means or graph-cut normalization in CHAMELEON. This record describes the original vector-data clustering rule and explicitly qualifies the faster representative-reuse and sampled-data enhancements. Recomputing representatives from all merged observations and selecting from old representatives need not give identical merges. claims.statement: Start with singleton clusters. Represent a cluster C by up to c selected points, with c a positive integer: choose the first farthest from its mean, then choose each next point to maximize its minimum distance to already selected points. Shrink every selected p to p+alpha(mean(C)−p), for a chosen shrink fraction in [0,1]. Define cluster distance as the minimum distance between a representative from each cluster, repeatedly merge the closest pair and stop at the requested count. In the original merge procedure recompute the mean with observation-count weights and select scattered points from the merged observations. The improved merge considers the at-most-2c old scattered points, recovered from their shrunken representatives when unshrinking is defined, and then shrinks new selections toward the merged mean. Large-data enhancements cluster a random sample, optionally partially cluster sample partitions before merging their partial clusters, and label remaining observations by the nearest selected final representative.

native_neighbors.name: ROCK clustering
native_neighbors.definition: An agglomerative clustering procedure that merges clusters using shared-neighbor link counts divided by a cluster-size normalization derived from a neighborhood model.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: ROCK is Guha et al.’s RObust Clustering using linKs procedure, designed for categorical or other similarity-based data. Links count common neighbors rather than direct similarities or graph cut weights. The normalized goodness is a heuristic and is not simply maximum shared-neighbor count. The record follows the 1999 conference article, not an uninspected expanded journal version. claims.statement: On the clustering sample choose a symmetric similarity in [0,1] and threshold theta. Define N(i)={j!=i:sim(i,j)>=theta} and link(i,j)=|N(i) intersect N(j)|; excluding each point from its own neighbor list reproduces the paper’s worked link counts. For clusters A,B set Link(A,B)=sum_(i in A,j in B)link(i,j). Starting from singletons, merge the pair maximizing g(A,B)=Link(A,B)/[(|A|+|B|)^(1+2f)−|A|^(1+2f)−|B|^(1+2f)]. The paper’s experimental configuration uses f(theta)=(1−theta)/(1+theta); use 0<=theta<1 so f>0 and the denominator is positive. Update cross-cluster links additively after a merge. Stop at the requested cluster count or when every remaining cross-cluster link count is zero. The optional large-data procedure clusters a random sample and labels other observations using representative subsets L_i, choosing the cluster maximizing its threshold-neighbor count divided by (|L_i|+1)^f.

native_neighbors.name: Neighbourhood components analysis
native_neighbors.definition: A supervised metric-learning algorithm that learns a linear transformation by maximizing the expected number of correctly classified training examples under stochastic leave-one-out neighbor selection.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: NCA is Goldberger et al.’s transformation-learning procedure, not ordinary k-nearest-neighbor voting or an unsupervised local-coordinate reconstruction. Its main objective sums correct-class probabilities; the paper also discusses a sum-of-log-probabilities alternative, which is a different objective. A rectangular transformation enables supervised dimensionality reduction. The AIO MetricLearning node is explicitly a deep neural network, so the original linear NCA procedure is not treated as its subclass. claims.statement: For labeled vectors x_i, choose a matrix A, possibly rectangular, and use squared transformed distance d_ij=||A(x_i−x_j)||², with Q=A^T A positive semidefinite. For j!=i set p_ij=exp(−d_ij)/sum_(k!=i)exp(−d_ik), and set p_ii=0. Define p_i=sum_(j:c_j=c_i)p_ij. Optimize f(A)=sum_i p_i by a gradient-based method; this is the expected number of correct labels when each training point selects one other point as its neighbor according to p_ij. For dimensionality reduction use A with d rows, store Ax_i and classify a new projected point using ordinary Euclidean k-nearest-neighbor voting. Learning the scale of A changes the softness of the training neighbor distribution; it does not uniquely determine the later integer k.

native_neighbors.name: Lifted structured embedding loss
native_neighbors.definition: A metric-learning objective that penalizes a positive pair’s Euclidean distance against negative distances incident to either endpoint, using a squared hinge and a hard maximum or its log-sum-exp relaxation.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: This record covers Song et al.’s lifted structured embedding loss, including the original maximum construction and the practically optimized log-sum-exp upper-bound form. These two forms are distinguished, not asserted numerically identical. The objective is separate from the full network, image preprocessing, hard-negative batch construction and optimizer. It is not N-pair-mc’s one-anchor dot-product categorical loss or N-pair-ovo’s sum of binary softplus comparisons. claims.statement: For labeled embeddings let D_ij=||z_i−z_j||_2. The original Equation (3) uses full-training-set positive pairs Phat and negative pairs Nhat. For positive (i,j), define J_ij=D_ij+max({alpha−D_ik:(i,k) in Nhat} union {alpha−D_jl:(j,l) in Nhat}), then average max(0,J_ij)^2 with divisor 2|Phat|. The practical Equation (4) instead uses a supplied minibatch: let P be its unordered same-class pairs and use Jtilde_ij=D_ij+log[sum_(k:y_k!=y_i)exp(alpha−D_ik)+sum_(l:y_l!=y_j)exp(alpha−D_jl)], summing only batch examples. Its loss is (1/(2|P|))sum_(i,j in P)max(0,Jtilde_ij)^2. Both endpoint-specific terms enter even when the same negative example belongs to both pools. Log-sum-exp bounds a hard maximum over the same terms; changing to a mined minibatch does not make its value a certified bound on the full-data objective. A dense pairwise distance matrix supports the batch computation. Loss distances are Euclidean norms, not squared distances; the squared matrix is only an intermediate.

native_neighbors.name: Locally Linear Embedding
native_neighbors.definition: A nonlinear dimensionality-reduction algorithm that learns sparse, sum-to-one linear reconstructions of each point from nearby points and computes embedding coordinates by minimizing reconstruction error with those same weights.
native_neighbors.identity_notes: LLE preserves local reconstruction relations rather than explicitly fitting all-pairs geodesic distances. It is distinct from Isomap, a linear PCA projection, Laplacian Eigenmaps, and a learned neural embedding layer. The expanded 2003 paper elaborates the same LLE identity; optional extensions are not automatically separate aliases. All 442 pinned AIO labels/scoped synonyms and 109 preceding native identities were compared, together with hidden/ignored-inclusive searches of both checkouts; source citations and pending frontier mentions were distinguished from existing concept identities.

claims.statement: Select neighbors, solve a constrained least-squares reconstruction for each input with weights zero outside its neighborhood and summing to one, then keep the weights fixed while minimizing embedded reconstruction error under centering and covariance constraints. The final step uses the smallest eigenmodes of (I − W)^T(I − W), excluding the constant translation mode. Weight regularization is needed for singular or poorly conditioned local fits.
